completedReview.finitePrintedRoutes: Choice is not a route (coordinator rule, 2026-10-12): when the candidate chooses N of M printed items and the scheme marks every choice alike, the question is ONE card printing all M items, with criteria per chosen slot and the scheme’s wording for every item. 27 such cards: 2014 Higher S3 Q1(C) and Q3(C); 2015 S3 Q5(B)(ii); 2016 S3 Q2(C); 2020 S3 Q1(B); 2021 S3 Q3(C); 2022 S3 Q6(C) and Q8(C); 2024 S3 Q7(C)(i) and Q8(B)(iii); 2021 Ordinary S2 Q6(E) and Q8(A); 2022 Ordinary S2 Q4(C) and Q6(A)(i); 2023 S2 Q1(E) and Q9(D); 2024 S2 Q3(C), Q4(C), Q4(E), Q6(C), Q7(B) and Q9(E); 2025 S2 Q1(A), Q2(D), Q9(D) and Q9(E); 2026 S2 Q8(B). Refinement (2026-10-12): a choose-one choice keeps one card per option only when the scheme marks the options differently or they file under different syllabus topics. All six Business choose-one questions share one grid and one topic, so each is one card too: 2015 Higher S3 Q4(A)(i) bar chart or line graph; 2022 S3 Q2(A) LTD or DAC; 2024 S3 Q3(C)(ii) one of three EU policies; 2023 Ordinary S2 Q6(E) assessors or actuaries; 2025 S2 Q3(E) one of three EU institutions; 2026 S2 Q3(A) bar chart or line graph; 2020 Ordinary S2 Q5(A)(ii) indemnity or utmost good faith; 2019 Ordinary S2 Q2(A) bar chart or line graph and S2 Q7(C) any three of five underlined sources of finance. 2018 Ordinary S2 Q5(A) any four of five underlined insurance terms, Q5(D) any three of four underlined recruitment terms and Q8(C) any three of four sources of finance are one card each. 2017 Ordinary S2 Q1(A) any two of three Consumer Protection Act provisions and Q6(A) any three of four underlined terms are one card each. 2015 Ordinary S2 Q5(B) any two of three principles of insurance is one card. 2013 Ordinary S2 Q8(C) any two of three product-development stages is one card. 2012 Ordinary S2 Q1(B) any three of four contract elements, Q5(B) any two of three principles of insurance, Q5(E) term loan or leasing and Q6(A) any two of three HR functions are one card each. 2011 Ordinary S2 Q4(E) the purpose of two of three PAYE forms and Q8(C)(ii) any two of the five levels of Maslow's hierarchy are one card each. 2010 Higher S3 Q3(C) any two of three EU policies is one card. Legacy IDs are kept as the one card; the 105 branch-only combination and option routes are gone (none reached main). candidateParser.evidenceLimit: Navigation aid only. Reviewed 2010-2026 Higher and 2010-2026 Ordinary papers reconcile with every parser leaf covered and no orphan. The census reads capitalised long-question heads ("QUESTION 1"), so the single-booklet 2010-2019 Ordinary papers count their Section 2, and it reads the 2019 Ordinary run-in head ("2." printed over an empty row above "3. Choose...", Q2's ask in a column beside the phone images) by moving that column under Q2; the repair is gated to Business and every other subject's census is byte-identical before and after. It also reads the 2011, 2013 and 2015 Ordinary Section 2 rubric that runs into its heading ("...either Part 1 or Part 2. PART 1"), which had read as Question 2 and filed Section 2 Q1 under Q2. And it reads a short-question head that opens its own paragraph inside a block after a bare word (2014 OL Q10 after "Surplus Deficit", Q12 after "Prototype Development"), which had made those questions vanish. The same split takes a head printed alone on its line with the ask below it (2011 OL Q2, 2012 OL Q6, 2013 OL Q2), unless the next block opens with that same head (the 2013 OL pyramid label "3."). And it reads the 2011 OL page 11 (Question 8), whose text layer is cut into overlapping vertical strips, from its characters rebuilt in reading order (strip_pages.py); no other Business page is strip-cut, and the selection scan reads the same rebuilt text. A matching table whose last term extracts alone, its explanation in the next block (2010 HL Q4 "5. Council of the European Union"), is read as a table row, not as Question 5, so the real Q5(a) is kept. Counts do not independently prove completion.
